canonical_definition: Code Generation is the task of producing executable code (typically Python) from natural language prompts or problem descriptions, often involving multi-step reasoning and adherence to test cases. It is commonly evaluated using benchmarks like HumanEval and MBPP (with metrics such as pass@1) to assess code intelligence, correctness, and problem-solving capabilities, though some papers frame it as part of real-world software development workflows or symbolic reasoning tasks. Inputs typically include programming problems or instructions, while outputs are code solutions validated via automated testing or execution. Variants include code completion, function-level generation, and integration with execution traces or domain-specific tasks like GeoQuery and NL2Bash.
